q: Growing different crops in turn on the same land is
e: Rotating crops keeps soil fertile and breaks pest cycles.

q: Which of these is a leguminous crop?
e: Cowpea is a legume.

q: The largest soil particles are
e: Sand has the largest soil particles.

q: Root nodules with nitrogen-fixing bacteria are found in
e: Legumes host nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules.

q: The rearing of bees is called
e: Apiculture means keeping bees.

q: Which of these is a ruminant?
e: Ruminants such as cattle chew the cud.

q: Which of these is a cereal crop?
e: Rice is a cereal grass crop.

q: Keeping fish in ponds is called
e: Fish farming is called aquaculture.

q: A soil with pH below 7 is
e: A pH below 7 means the soil is acidic.

q: Manure is best described as
e: Manure is organic fertiliser from animal waste or plant matter.

q: The main purpose of weeding is to
e: Weeds compete with crops for water, light and nutrients.

q: A castrated male cattle is called a
e: A castrated male cattle is a steer.

q: The layer of soil richest in humus is the
e: The topsoil holds most organic matter and nutrients.

q: Loamy soil is a mixture of
e: Loam is regarded as the best agricultural soil.

q: Which of these is a nitrogen fertiliser?
e: Urea is rich in nitrogen.

q: NPK fertiliser supplies
e: N is nitrogen, P is phosphorus and K is potassium.

q: Lime is applied to soil to
e: Lime neutralises acidic soils.

q: Which of these is a root tuber?
e: Cassava is a root tuber crop.

q: Which of these is a cereal?
e: Rice is a cereal grain.

q: Cocoa in Nigeria is mainly grown as a
e: Cocoa is grown mainly for sale and export.

q: A cover crop is planted mainly to
e: Ground cover reduces erosion and keeps the soil moist.

q: Mulching is the covering of the soil with
e: Mulch reduces evaporation and suppresses weeds.

q: Chemicals used to kill weeds are called
e: Herbicides kill weeds.

q: Cassava is commonly propagated by
e: Pieces of cassava stem are planted to grow new plants.

q: Newcastle disease affects
e: Newcastle disease is a viral disease of birds.

q: Nagana in cattle is spread by the
e: Tsetse flies transmit the trypanosomes that cause nagana.

q: Which breed of cattle is kept mainly for milk?
e: The Friesian is a high-yielding dairy breed.

q: Birds kept mainly for egg production are called
e: Layers produce eggs; broilers are raised for meat.

q: Day-old chicks are kept warm in a
e: A brooder supplies heat to young chicks.

q: In which poultry system do birds roam freely outdoors?
e: Free-range birds move about outside.

q: Fish farming is also called
e: Pisciculture is the rearing of fish.

q: Horticulture is the cultivation of
e: Horticulture covers garden crops.

q: A land tenure system in which land belongs to the family or community is
e: Communal ownership is common in many parts of Nigeria.

q: The Land Use Act of 1978 vests land in each state in the
e: The governor holds land in trust for the people.

q: Farm records are kept mainly to
e: Records show profit, loss and where to improve.

q: Irrigation is the
o: artificial supply of water to crops
e: Irrigation waters crops when rain is not enough.

q: Fallowing means
o: leaving land uncultivated to regain fertility
e: Rest allows the soil to recover.

q: In shifting cultivation, farmers
o: farm the same plot for ever
move to new land when the soil loses fertility
e: Land is abandoned after a few seasons and left to recover.

q: A tool used for digging and weeding by hand is the
e: The hoe is a basic hand tool for tillage and weeding.

q: Silage is
e: Silage is green fodder preserved by fermentation for feeding animals.

q: Which soil type has the highest water-holding capacity?
e: Clay has very fine particles and many tiny pores that hold water strongly.

q: The conversion of ammonium compounds in the soil to nitrates by bacteria is called
e: Nitrifying bacteria such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter oxidise ammonium to nitrate.

q: Which of these diseases is caused by a fungus and attacks cocoa pods?
e: Black pod is caused by the fungus Phytophthora palmivora.

q: Cassava mosaic disease is spread mainly by
e: The whitefly Bemisia tabaci transmits the cassava mosaic virus.

q: A farmer harvested 4,500 kg of maize from 3 hectares. The yield per hectare is
e: Yield per hectare = 4,500 / 3 = 1,500 kg.

q: The average gestation period of a sow is about
e: Pigs are pregnant for roughly 3 months, 3 weeks and 3 days, about 114 days.

q: The first and largest compartment of the stomach of a cow is the
e: The rumen is the largest chamber where microbial fermentation of fibre takes place.

q: Which of the following is a principle of co-operative societies?
o: Profit goes to the chairman alone
e: Co-operatives admit members voluntarily and operate one member, one vote.

q: A broiler flock consumed 150 kg of feed and gained 50 kg in body weight. The feed conversion ratio is
e: FCR = feed eaten / weight gained = 150 / 50 = 3.

q: Foot-and-mouth disease in cattle is caused by a
e: Foot-and-mouth disease is caused by a highly contagious virus.

q: Which of these tools is used for levelling the soil surface after tillage?
e: A rake breaks clods and levels the seedbed.

q: Which implement is used for primary tillage on a large farm?
e: The plough is the first implement to cut and turn the soil.

q: A farmer sold his produce for N120,000 after spending N85,000 on production. His profit is
e: Profit = revenue minus total cost = 120,000 - 85,000 = N35,000.

q: Striga (witchweed) is a weed that
e: Striga attaches to the roots of maize, sorghum and millet and steals nutrients.

q: A heterozygous tall plant (Tt) is crossed with a dwarf plant (tt). The expected ratio of tall to dwarf offspring is
e: Tt x tt gives Tt and tt in equal numbers, a 1:1 ratio.

q: Yellowing of leaves (chlorosis) in crops is a common sign of deficiency of
e: Nitrogen is needed for chlorophyll, so its lack causes pale yellow leaves.

q: An agricultural extension agent mainly serves as a link between
e: Extension agents carry research findings to farmers and bring farmers' problems back to researchers.

q: Afforestation means
o: Planting trees where there was no forest before
e: Afforestation is establishing forest on land that was not previously forested.

q: If 25 out of 500 chicks died in a brooder, the mortality rate is
e: Mortality = 25/500 x 100 = 5%.

q: Which breed of chicken is a dual-purpose breed?
e: Rhode Island Red is kept for both eggs and meat.

q: Which fish is commonly cultured in ponds in Nigeria?
e: Clarias catfish is hardy and widely raised in freshwater ponds.

q: The law of diminishing returns states that
o: Output rises forever as input rises
Extra units of input eventually give smaller extra output
e: Adding more of one input to fixed others eventually yields smaller additions to output.

q: Which breed of cattle is trypanotolerant?
e: N'Dama cattle resist trypanosomiasis in tsetse-infested areas.

q: A common insect pest of stored grains is the
e: Weevils feed on grains in storage and cause heavy losses.

q: Which of the following is a fixed asset on a farm?
e: A tractor is durable and used over many seasons, unlike inputs consumed in one season.

q: A farmer uses a seed rate of 20 kg per hectare. The seed needed for 2.5 hectares is
e: Seed needed = 20 x 2.5 = 50 kg.

q: The first milk produced by a cow after calving is called
e: Colostrum is rich in antibodies and essential for the newborn calf.

q: The best method of controlling erosion on a sloping farmland is
o: Ploughing up and down the slope
e: Ploughing along the contour slows runoff and reduces soil loss.

q: The increased vigour of offspring over their parents resulting from crossing unrelated parents is called
e: Hybrid vigour, or heterosis, is the superior performance of crossbred offspring.

q: Night blindness in farm animals and humans is caused by deficiency of
e: Vitamin A is needed for the retina to work in dim light.
